assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation is a clear mechanistic principle (heterobifunctional molecules or glues hijack E3 ligases to eliminate rather than inhibit a target) that opens a genuinely new therapeutic modality and previously undruggable targets. Chemistry-centred, with broad generative potential and a story that can be explained to a general audience.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli made the first VHL-based small-molecule PROTACs and structural basis of ternary complexes. The molecular glue branch (Handa, Ito, thalidomide and cereblon) is a distinct discovery and would crowd a three-person citation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is accumulating (degraders in late-stage trials) but no approved PROTAC drug is certain as far as I know; the concept itself is well confirmed by many independent groups. Timing is plausible, slightly early on the clinical side.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs only or also include cereblon and molecular glues.
Clinical status is from my memory and not verified.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto and Ciulli is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a workhorse transformation in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with an enabling ligand design principle. Impact is vast and durable, though the field was previously recognised via the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination and ligand families; Kosugi/Migita tin-amide precedent is a historical antecedent and is a three-way question, but two laureates give a clean citation.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, thoroughly confirmed over thirty years; recognition is arguably overdue, with a concern that it is seen as an extension of 2010.
uncertainties: Overlap in public perception with the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Weight of the Kosugi and Migita precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle of the cell is a physically clear, quantitative concept (condensate thermodynamics, scaling and material properties) with huge conceptual reach across cell biology and disease. Appeals strongly to a physicist's lens.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman reported P granules as liquid droplets (2009); Rosen showed multivalent-interaction driven phase transitions (2012). Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory and sequence grammar. A fair trio is feasible but the list is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted, but debate remains about physiological relevance, definition of 'condensate' and in vivo evidence, so the interpretation is still moving.
uncertainties: Whether this is chemistry versus physiology/medicine.
Unsettled physiological relevance of some condensates.
Credit among Pappu, Mittag, Rosen and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule electrical readout of nucleic acids through nanopores is physically elegant and delivered long-read, portable sequencing. Combines nanoscale physics, protein engineering and chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon, Branton and Deamer (1996) demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Akeson showed enzyme-controlled ratcheting; Bayley engineered pores. I am unsure of the current status (alive or not) of Branton and Bayley, which affects feasibility. Commercial realisation involved others (e.g. Oxford Nanopore) not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and widely used, with independent confirmation; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Survival status of some credited names is unverified by me.
Fit with chemistry rather than physics or physiology/medicine.
Three-person limit forces difficult attribution among five names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite photovoltaics rose from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency in a decade, an extraordinary materials-chemistry and device story with a clear physical basis (defect tolerance, long carrier lengths).
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite sensitised cells (2009); Park and Snaith achieved solid-state cells and efficiency leaps (2012). Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok are also prominent, so attribution is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is strongly confirmed, but long-term stability and commercialisation are not settled, which makes timing arguably premature.
uncertainties: Contested credit across at least six people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs uses diffraction-before-destruction to record room-temperature structures and time-resolved dynamics, a new capability grounded in clear physics and aligned with chemistry's interest in structure and dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu and Neutze proposed the concept; Chapman led the first experiments with Fromme and Schlichting contributions. Neutze is not in the credited list; the credited set may omit key conceptual contributors.
assessment.maturity: Method is established and replicated at multiple facilities; new chemistry results are accumulating, with recognition plausible but the main impact is still growing.
uncertainties: Absence of some conceptual originators from the credited names.
Whether the impact on chemistry is yet decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoding noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs gives chemists a general way to put new functionality into proteins in living cells, a clear and generative capability.
assessment.attribution: Schultz led the first systematic work in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended to multiple codons and animals; Wang made early contributions. Seems a fair trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used for two decades, with extensive independent confirmation; recognition would be timely, though therapeutic payoff remains modest.
uncertainties: Breadth of practical impact beyond research tools.
Relative credit of Wang versus Yokoyama and Mehl.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and dynamics, enabling ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces and reactions. A clear principle (extended Lagrangian) with large lasting impact; the follow-on metadynamics adds to Parrinello's overall significance.
assessment.attribution: Credit sits unambiguously with Car and Parrinello (1985), producing a clean two-person citation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and broadly confirmed, although much current practice has moved on to Born-Oppenheimer variants, and the field was recognised by the 2013 computational prize and 1998 DFT prize.
uncertainties: Prior computational-chemistry prizes may reduce priority.
Whether recognition might favour Parrinello's broader body of work including metadynamics.
